target_body: Promo test: paid conversions +31%, monthly rev +18%, low-touch seg, later-cycle retention -12pp; not a repeatable win for planning.
system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Promo test: paid conversions +31%, monthly rev +18%, low-touch seg, later-cycle retention -12pp; not a repeatable win for planning.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

memory_block.body: Promo test: paid conversions +31%, monthly rev +18%, low-touch seg, later-cycle retention -12pp; not a repeatable win for planning.
Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.
Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.
Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.
Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

answer.rationale:
The two live symptoms (onboarding completion -4pp, activation -6pp) are upstream funnel problems, and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so fixing it plausibly addresses both. memory_86 and memory_31 both point at signup/onboarding friction, and memory_31 is the only inherited claim that explicitly asserts durability. I am deliberately NOT chasing the competitor's price move: memory_73 is the cautionary case where a headline conversion/revenue win (+31%/+18%) masked -12pp later-cycle retention, which is exactly the wrong trade against a 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective; that memory is trustworthy enough as a warning that I don't need to spend budget re-verifying it. Referral (memory_57) is clean but targets established customers and does nothing for the activation/onboarding decline; enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is a different segment than the one being lost.

Verification is spent on the weakest links rather than the strongest. memory_86 is the primary support for my intended action but it is stated purely in proxy terms ('completion rates', 'time-to-value', 'early product adoption') with no retention or revenue readout - the same shape of claim that memory_73 shows can invert downstream. memory_91 is the leading alternative and is even softer ('week-one engagement', 'first meaningful action'), so verifying it tells me whether to switch cheaply. I skip re-pulling memory_31 because it already carries the durability qualifier I would be checking for.

Key uncertainty I cannot resolve from the inherited summaries: whether these lifts were measured on the same self-serve SMB cohort now under competitive pressure, whether they were ever attributed to retained qualified revenue rather than funnel proxies, and whether the current declines are demand-mix shifts (competitor siphoning price-sensitive accounts) rather than friction - in which case removing friction just admits lower-intent accounts faster. Downstream risk is real and specific: stripping onboarding steps can both degrade qualification signal and cannibalize the demo-request path that memory_44 says outperforms for enterprise. So the test should be scoped to self-serve SMB, leave the enterprise/demo route untouched, and be instrumented on retained qualified revenue and later-cycle retention as primary guardrails, not completion rate. If verification shows memory_86 was proxy-only and unreplicated, I will fall back to activation_messaging as the lower-blast-radius option.
